text: Update: the 38 route got rerouted this month, so now I switch to the 5 at Civic Center instead of transferring at Van Ness. It actually shaves about ten minutes off, so I'm down to roughly forty minutes each way.
My manager moved our standup to 9:15, which means I can catch the earlier bus and still make it with time to spare. Mornings feel a lot less rushed now.
Started physio for the IT band thing. The therapist gave me a set of glute exercises to do three times a week, and said I should hold off on running more than 5k until the pain settles.
I tried the foam roller routine she recommended before bed and my knee was noticeably less stiff the next morning.
I've been meal-prepping lentils and rice on Sundays. It's brought my weekly grocery spend down to about sixty dollars, which is a big drop from before.
Splurged on a decent chef's knife this week. It was forty dollars but honestly it's already made cooking feel less like a chore.
The landlord finally fixed the radiator, so the apartment actually holds heat now. With the cold snap this week that's made a real difference at night.
It's been raining most of the week and the bus shelter at Civic Center actually has a roof, unlike the old Van Ness stop, so I've stayed dry waiting for the transfer.
I joined a Tuesday-evening pottery class at the community center. It's two hours and it's become the thing I most look forward to in the week.
My sister is visiting next month and staying for a long weekend, so I've been clearing out the spare room to set up an air mattress for her.
I adopted a cat from the shelter — her name is Pekoe and she's about two years old. The adoption fee was eighty-five dollars and included her shots.
Pekoe has decided the windowsill by my desk is hers, which means I now have a small audience during every work call.
